answer_to_the_main_question.short: Yes to the first half, and yes to the second half, and they are disjoint: each reddens only for its own reason. The emitter half (missing `actor`) is caught by the new Python row alone - with the actor removed, pytest reddens KeyError: 'actor' while node unit stays 30/30 and the node e2e stays green. The filter half is caught by the node tests alone - a filter that treats the director's own ack as input reddens the e2e at 'an own ack tick must not start a turn' (6 !== 5) while unit stays 30/30, and the authorless-driver_id filter mutant reddens node unit + e2e while pytest stays 2/2.
answer_to_the_main_question.why_two_languages_are_needed: The node suites hand-build the payloads they feed ownEchoOnly, so no node test can observe the real Python emitter; the Python row never runs the JS filter, so no pytest row can observe the filter. Measured both ways below (M1 and M5).
answer_to_the_main_question.contract_is_only_a_literal: The join between the halves is the string format 'driver:<id>': the emitter writes self.actor, the row pins the literal 'driver:bob', the filter concatenates 'driver:' + driverId, the unit table pins 'driver:dsh-x'. No single test spans both sides; see unverified and M1b.

criteria.summary: No assertion was weakened or made vacuous and no other wake source is reachable by the change. Two notes: (1) driver.md's inserted paragraph leaves a sentence fragment that is injected verbatim into the director's system prompt; (2) the new Python row pins 'an actor field equal to driver:<id> for driver callers', which a guess ('driver:'+acker) also satisfies - it cannot see the owner-browser principal (M1b).

evidence.no_weakened_assertion: Read the whole diff. The only removed rows are the parent's `[own, claim, acked({driver_id only})] -> true` and `[ev({actor:null, driver_id:me})] -> true` ('null actor falls back to driver_id'); both are replaced by rows asserting false, which is the fix itself, plus four stricter ack rows and one extra 'someone else's lease expiry' assertion. Every retained row and every e2e assertion is unchanged. The e2e kept 'an own-writes tick must never reach the session' and 'a foreign tick is delivered'.
evidence.e2e_ack_assertion_is_not_vacuous: It is a 500 ms window plus a later delivered('delivery-1')===undefined check. M5 makes the filter exempt director_message_acked and the e2e reddens at exactly that line in 2.7 s, so the window is wide enough to catch a real wake on this fixture.
evidence.other_wake_sources_untouched: ownEchoOnly has exactly one call site (runtime.onEvent, runtime.mjs:740). watch_process completion notices (694), idle-review notification (939) and both todo handbacks (979, 993) call notify() directly, below no echo filter. wakeSources and endsDormancy (runtime.mjs:105-108) have no hunk, and their unit row ('only real input ends dormancy' incl. agent-message, subagent-settled, child) passes 30/30.
evidence.worker_own_write_cannot_hide_a_result: A native child shares the director's token, so its State write is stamped driver:<director> and is silenced as an own echo - intended, the director caused it. The result still arrives: child settlement is a DSH session message with source kind child/subagent-settled, which never passes through ownEchoOnly and is a wake source by endsDormancy. A worker on another driver identity is foreign and wakes. Verified by reading the single call site and the wake-source table; not exercised by an e2e where a child writes State and then settles (see unverified).
evidence.note_driver_md: integrations/dsh-driver/driver.md:100-106 now reads '... (including new issues). Your own writes carry your actor - including your acknowledge and resolve of a message - so a tick of only those does not wake you. An event with no actor is a system event (...), so it always reaches you, whatever ids it names; an event naming you is not your own write unless its actor says so.' followed by a new line 'project/driver inbox messages, and native worker messages/completion.' The insertion split the original sentence 'The runtime stays subscribed to project State changes (including new issues), project/driver inbox messages, and native worker messages/completion.' - line 106 is now an orphaned fragment starting lowercase after a full stop, and it is part of the system prompt the director reads. Content of the inserted rule is correct against the code; only the stitching is broken. Cosmetic, not criterion-blocking, but it is a shipped prompt defect.
evidence.note_owner_browser_sentence: The brief asks whether stamping self.actor rather than 'driver:'+acker is wrong because _acker() (core/director_messaging.py:254-265) returns bare 'owner' for owner-browser callers. It is not wrong. Measured: a driver ack stores {driver_id:'bob', actor:'driver:bob'}; an owner-browser ack stores {driver_id:'owner', actor:'owner:human@example.test'}. Under the filter, the owner ack is not 'driver:<director>' and therefore wakes the director - which is correct, because a human in the dashboard acted, not the director; and 'driver:'+acker would have produced the false principal 'driver:owner' while waking exactly the same way. The emitter records what the transaction actually authenticated, and driver_id keeps the legacy 'owner' marker the ack tables read.

unverified: No shipped test spans the emitter->filter boundary: the Python row never runs the JS filter and the node suites never run the Python emitter. The join is the literal 'driver:<id>' duplicated in two languages, which is why M1 and M5 each redden in one language only. A single cross-language test would be strictly better; none exists in this range.

'A worker's own State write going silent cannot hide a result' is established by reading the single ownEchoOnly call site (runtime.mjs:740) and the untouched wake-source table, not by a runtime e2e in which a native child writes State under the director's identity and then settles. A test for that shape does not exist.

The 500 ms settle window in the new e2e ack case is a timing assumption. M5 shows it fires within 2.7 s of test time (the assertion trips), so the window is adequate on this fixture, but on a loaded host a wake slower than 500 ms would be caught only by the later delivered('delivery-1')===undefined assertion, which is checked after the foreign turn.

Cursor persistence after a silent tick: the e2e measures the in-memory cursor (next long poll uses after=11/12/13) and pump() writes cursor.json unconditionally after onEvent returns, but no test restarts the process after a silent tick to prove the file matches.
Principal strings other than driver:<id> and owner:<email> (e.g. system:, anonymous, dshr-* recovery actors) were not enumerated; only the two paths above were measured against the filter.

pytest scope was the changed row's file plus three neighbouring director-messaging modules (86 passed). The full repository suite was not run, and no AItelier pytest ran on the host or in the production container.
The driver.md fragment defect is reported, not fixed: this review commits only its report.
